_comment: Curated A11 test-point data. Hand-authored from the 1996 Series II service manual
and from the Figure 7-11 schematic sheets, not parsed.
A11 generates no supply that Chapter 2 tabulates. It consumes the FR1, FR2, S, LH
and RLH rails made by the Regulator/Guard Crossing assembly (A17) and the Digital
Power Supply (A19), so there is no Table 2-x for it and every expectation below
comes from §5-13 to §5-16, from the diagnostic fault codes of §5-2, or from an
annotation printed on the schematic.
Signal names and their sheet/zone references are transcribed from the legend box on
schematic sheet 1, which prints them as 'TP2 = REF13 (PG2 C7)' -- page 2, zone C7.
Every one was checked a second way, against the label printed beside the flag symbol
on the net itself, and all twelve agree.
The twelve test points are two physically different things and the schematic says
which is which with two different symbols. Six are non-insulated wire loops, Table
6-12 'TP1,TP3 TP8-10, TP12  JUMPER,WIRE,NONINSUL,0.200CTR', stock 816090, and they
take a clip lead. The other six -- TP2, TP4, TP5, TP6, TP7, TP11 -- are plated
through holes with no parts-list line at all, and they take a probe tip. The parts
list and the schematic symbols agree exactly on the split.
Five of the twelve carry no number, and that is the manual's position rather than a
gap here. TP4, TP5, TP6 and TP7 are oscilloscope points: §5-13 and §5-14 check them
against Figures 5-17 to 5-21 and against a duty cycle that changes with the output
setting, and the note on Figure 5-20 says outright that the duty cycle may differ
from the figure. Sheet 2 does annotate their amplitudes -- 0 to 18 V at TP4, 0 to 5 V
at TP6, 0 to 3 V at TP7 -- and those are recorded in the notes, but an amplitude is
not an acceptance band and writing one in would score a good board as failing. TP11
is checked only relative to TP9 and TP10, so it has no absolute value either.
TP3 (REFCOM MECCA POINT) is the common for most of the procedure; TP12 (ADCCOM) is
the common for the adc circuit and TP1 (SCOM) for the duty-cycle logic. Watch which
one a step asks for -- §5-13 alone uses all three.
Citation convention: §5-13's printed step numbers are the ones used here, because
the combined procedure leaves them unchanged. For §5-14, §5-15 and §5-16 the source
cites the combined step number the app shows and the note gives the printed one, so
that the app's own step-matching cannot attach an expectation to the wrong step.
See the procedure caveat in a11.reference.json.

testpoints.note: S COM, the common of the ±17 S and ±44 S supplies that arrive at P402 from the Regulator/Guard Crossing assembly (A17). It is the common §5-14 asks for in its first four steps and the one §5-16 asks for on both of its, so it is not interchangeable with TP3: the duty-cycle logic and the adc reference chain sit on different returns from the reference circuit.

testpoints.condition: Powered up. The manual notes drift while the assembly warms up; the hybrid oven has to reach 62 °C first.
testpoints.note: The 13 V reference itself, at pin 12 of the HR5 Reference Hybrid, ahead of R12. Published as 'between +13 and +14 V and very stable', so the band here is 13.5 ±0.5 V. This is the amplitude the first duty-cycle channel switches, which makes it the amplitude every DAC output is a fraction of -- §2-101 works the example out as (duty × 13 V) + (duty × 0.78 mV). If it is wrong, §5-13 step 2 says to check the supplies going into HR5 before condemning the hybrid: HR5 is stock 893334 and not field-repairable. Fault code 2817 checks the same reference by nulling the DAC against it and trips at 10 %.

testpoints.source: Figure 7-11 sheet 1 legend (PG2 C6); §5-13 steps 2–11 and 14–16
testpoints.note: The star ('mecca') point where the reference circuit's return is defined, and the common for most of §5-13 and all of §5-15's high-impedance checks. Two exceptions are printed in the same section: step 12 references TP8 to TP12 instead, and §5-15 references the adc circuit to TP12 throughout.

testpoints.condition: Scope at 10 V/div, 2 ms/div. Checked twice: at 0 V output (Figure 5-18) and at 6.5 V dc operate, where the duty cycle should be about 50 % (Figure 5-19).
testpoints.source: §5-13 step 4; also step 26 of the combined procedure
testpoints.note: The gate drive for the first channel's series switches Q4 and Q5. It is the one channel-one signal that is not TTL: U14's Q1* output is amplified by Q33, Q34, VR11, VR12 and R44–R46 so that it swings 0 to 18 V, which sheet 2 annotates on the net. Printed as §5-14 step 10. The square wave runs at 190 Hz and its duty cycle is the DAC's output setting, so the trace changes as soon as the output is changed -- that is the check, not a level.

testpoints.condition: 6.5 V dc, operate. Scope at 5 V/div, 2 ms/div (Figure 5-21).
testpoints.note: The first channel as it is presented to the five-pole filter on the DAC Filter SIP (A11A1) -- the node where series switch Q5 and shunt switch Q6 meet. This is the waveform the whole DAC accuracy argument rests on: the filter averages it, so its amplitude must be exactly the 13 V reference and its dc resistance to TP2 must look like zero, which is what the series linearity control circuit around U38 and Z2 is for.

testpoints.condition: Scope at 2 V/div, 2 ms/div. §5-13 step 3 checks it against Figure 5-17 with common on TP3; the duty-cycle section rechecks it at 6.5 V dc operate against Figure 5-25.
testpoints.source: §5-13 step 3; also step 25 of the combined procedure
testpoints.note: Gate drive for the first channel's shunt switch Q6, made by Q35 inverting U14's Q1* output. Sheet 2 annotates the net 0 to 5 V. Printed as §5-14 step 9, which names Q35 as the suspect. A wrong signal here is the first fork in §5-13: step 3 sends you straight to the duty-cycle control circuit rather than further down the DAC.

testpoints.condition: 6.5 V dc, operate. Scope at 2 V/div, 2 ms/div (Figure 5-20).
testpoints.source: §5-13 step 5; also step 29 of the combined procedure
testpoints.note: The second (fine) channel's input to the filter, switched between roughly 0.78 mV and 0 V by FETs Q30 and Q32 from the 3 V source that U11 buffers. Sheet 2 annotates the net 0 to 3 V, which is the amplitude before the ×3800 divider in HR5 -- the 0.78 mV the filter actually sees is not measurable here. The manual prints a note under Figure 5-20 saying the duty cycle may differ from the figure, and gives a better test than any trace: turn the edit knob to vary the second least significant digit of the output and watch the duty cycle here change. Printed as §5-14 step 13.

testpoints.conflict: The three steps that measure TP8 do not agree on the common. Step 12 prints '(common to TP12)', steps 14 and 16 print '(common to TP3)'. TP12 is ADCCOM and TP3 is REFCOM MECCA POINT; the DAC output is defined against REFCOM, and the difference between the two is exactly the sort of small offset a ±0.25 V check will not reveal. TP3 is used here and step 12's TP12 is recorded rather than followed.
testpoints.note: The DAC's own output, sensed at the assembly. This is the voltage every other analog board is calibrated against, so a reading here that is right ends the search on A11 and starts it on the Switch Matrix. Note the tolerances are 'for an uncalibrated instrument' -- a calibrated one should be far closer, and §5-13 step 16 exploits that by comparing this node against the front-panel binding post to ±10 ppm, which is the sense current cancellation check.

states.label: -10 V dc, operate (11 V range)
states.setup: Same step: set the output to -10 V dc and read TP8 again. The polarity is switched by K1 and K2, so a failure on one polarity only is a relay or its driver.

states.label: 20 V dc, operate (22 V range)
states.setup: Set the output to 20 V dc, operate. RANGE SELECT switches the output stage to a gain of two.

testpoints.note: The noninverting input of the adc amplifier, switched between ADC COM, RCL and DAC SENSE CAL by relays K6 and K7. Printed as §5-15 step 12, which gives 'a nominal 6.3V dc which is the voltage on the RCL line' and no band at all; the ±5 % here is a working figure and is marked inferred for that reason. What the step really establishes is that K6 and K7 have selected RCL. VR17, VR18, VR21 and VR22 clamp both inputs, so a reading pinned near a zener voltage is a clamp conducting rather than a signal.

The inverting input of the adc amplifier, switched between DAC SENSE CAL and REFCAL by relay K5. Printed as §5-15 step 11, which gives 'a nominal 6.3V dc which is the output of the DAC' and no band, so the ±5 % is inferred as on TP9. K5 is also what connects the references on the Buffered Reference SIP (A11A2) into the null measurement, which is how fault codes 2814 to 2817 read them.

testpoints.condition: 2 V at 1 kHz, operate. Read TP9 with common on TP10 first, note it, then read TP11 with common on TP12.
testpoints.note: The adc amplifier's output, tied to ADC AMP OUT. It has no absolute expectation because the published check is a ratio: TP11 must be 11 times the TP9-to-TP10 difference, within ±15 mV. §2-113 gives the same rule as (noninverting − inverting) × 11, and VR19 and VR20 clamp the output at ±4 V, so the gain check has to be done at a small input or the clamps take over. Printed as §5-15 step 13; fault code 2808 makes the same measurement in software and trips at ±5 % of the gain.

ADC COM, the common of the adc and adc amplifier section, clamped to SCOM by the back-to-back pair CR4 and CR5 so the two grounds cannot drift far apart. Every §5-15 step except the three supply checks references here.

probePoints.label: U38 pin 6 (series linearity control)
probePoints.note: Published as +23.0 to +26.4 V. U38 with resistor network Z2 and a 19.996 kΩ resistor inside HR5 supplies the filter current that would otherwise flow through series switch Q5, which has 3 to 5 Ω of on-resistance. That is what makes the path from TP2 to TP5 look like zero ohms and keeps the DAC linear.

probePoints.label: U2 pin 1 (negative offset circuit)
probePoints.note: Published as -13 to -14 V, which is the 13 V reference inverted. U2A and two 20 kΩ resistors in HR6 form a unity-gain inverter; its output is then divided in HR5 to about -127 mV at the filter input. The offset exists so that a DAC output of 0 V still needs a first-channel count of about 400, which guarantees a minimum pulse width of roughly 50 µs -- without it the reference would not have time to settle after being switched in.

probePoints.label: TP1 on the DAC Filter SIP (A11A1)
probePoints.condition: 6.5 V dc, operate. Common on TP3 of the main board, not on the SIP.
probePoints.note: The filter output, measured on the plug-in DAC Filter SIP itself and not on this board -- A11 has its own TP1 (SCOM) and it is a different point entirely. Published as a nominal +6.5 V dc ±0.1 V for an uncalibrated instrument, free of distortion and stable. The filter's dominant pole is near 10 Hz, which gives 120 dB of rejection at the 190 Hz switching rate, so any ripple visible here is a filter fault. §2-105 notes the SIP also makes the 15 V rail that R111 uses to pull up RANGE SELECT.

probePoints.label: HR6 pin 18 (DC amp hybrid output)
probePoints.condition: 10 V dc, operate.
probePoints.note: The dc amplifier hybrid's output, ahead of the output buffer. Published as a nominal +10 V dc ±0.25 V for an uncalibrated instrument. HR6 is a precision op amp on a heated ceramic substrate bonded to a resistor network and held at 50 °C by the sheet 1 heater circuit through Q3; step 10 says to suspect that heater control as well as the hybrid, and fault 2804 is the code that fires when either oven falls out of regulation.

probePoints.label: L10 (output buffer output)
probePoints.condition: 10 V dc, operate.
probePoints.note: The output buffer U5's output at the L10 choke, which is where the DAC's current drive is finally developed. Published as a nominal +10 V dc ±0.25 V for an uncalibrated instrument. U5 is inside HR6's feedback loop, so the dc accuracy is the hybrid's and only the drive is U5's; it current-limits at about 60 mA through the R23 sense resistor and the Q10 / Q8 / Q11 chain.

probePoints.label: U37 pin 7 (RANGE SELECT)
probePoints.note: The RANGE SELECT control line on the analog side of opto-isolator U37, pulled up by R111 to the 15 V made on the DAC Filter SIP. It configures the output stage for unity gain (11 V range) or a gain of two (22 V range) by switching Q20, Q21 and Q15 and the 40 kΩ feedback resistors in HR6. The two published levels are far apart, so this is one of the easier faults on the board to confirm.

states.label: 22 V range (20 V, operate)
states.setup: Set the Calibrator to 20 V, operate, and read the same pin.

probePoints.label: U2 pin 7 (shunt linearity control)
probePoints.condition: 10 V dc, operate, then 20 V dc, operate. The reading must be the same in both ranges.
probePoints.note: Published as a nominal -10 V dc, ±0.35 V for an uncalibrated instrument and ±0.1 V for a calibrated one; the wider band is used here. U2B is an inverting amplifier of gain 1 in the 11 V range and 0.5 in the 22 V range, set by Q22 and three 80 kΩ resistors in HR6 -- which is exactly why the reading must not move when the range changes. It cancels the current that would otherwise flow in shunt switch Q6, making that switch look like 0 Ω.

probePoints.label: U6 pin 10 (8 MHz clock in)
probePoints.condition: Scope at 2 V/div, 100 ns/div (Figure 5-22). Common on TP1, not TP3.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-14 step 1. The TTL 8 MHz clock that the 82C54 interval timer runs on. It arrives from the Regulator/Guard Crossing assembly (A17) as a differential 400 mV p-p pair, CLK and CLK*, and comparator U7 squares it up; the same low-level pair is separately isolated by transformer T1 and squared by U10 for the U14 flip-flop. A dead clock here does not simply stop the DAC -- the watchdog around U15, C63 and R48 forces the first channel filter input to REFCOM, so the DAC goes to zero rather than to something arbitrary.

probePoints.label: U6 pin 16 (OUT1, first channel)
probePoints.condition: 6.5 V dc, operate. Scope at 2 V/div, 2 ms/div. TTL square wave, about 50 % duty cycle.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-14 step 2. OUT1 of the 82C54 is the first channel: its duty cycle is the DAC's coarse setting, and 6.5 V out of a 13 V reference is why the manual asks for 50 % here. The duty-cycle resolution is 0.0024 %, which is 0.309 mV at the DAC output. §5-14 step 2 says to check all of U6's control lines and not just the chip.

probePoints.label: U6 pin 20 (OUT2, second channel)
probePoints.condition: 6.5 V dc, operate. Scope at 2 V/div, 2 ms/div. TTL square wave.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-14 step 3. OUT2 is the second (fine) channel, worth 18.5 nV per count at the DAC output. No duty cycle is specified because the fine channel's setting depends on the digits below the coarse channel's resolution. If this is wrong the step says U6 itself is probably at fault.

probePoints.label: U13 pin 6 (CH1 FLOATING)
probePoints.condition: 6.5 V dc, operate. Scope at 2 V/div, 2 ms/div (Figure 5-23).
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-14 step 4. The first channel after the 20 MHz optocoupler U13 has crossed it into the floating reference section. The isolation matters as much as the waveform: everything downstream of here sits on REFCOM, not on the logic common.

probePoints.label: U10 pin 4 (8 MHz clock, floating side)
probePoints.condition: Scope at 2 V/div, 100 ns/div (Figure 5-24).
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-14 step 5. The clock as it exists on the floating side, after transformer T1 has isolated the low-level CLK/CLK* pair and comparator U10 has squared it. Note the common changes here: the step prints TP3, where the four steps before it print TP1. This clock is what re-times CH1 FLOATING through the U14 flip-flop, so jitter here becomes a DAC linearity error rather than a logic failure.

probePoints.label: U14 pin 8 (watchdog 4 MHz clock)
probePoints.condition: TTL level 4 MHz clock.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-14 step 6. The second half of the U14 dual flip-flop divides the 8 MHz clock by two to make the 4 MHz the watchdog one-shot is retriggered by. This is the clock whose loss the watchdog is watching for.

probePoints.label: U15 pin 13 (watchdog timer output)
probePoints.condition: Constant logic high while the 4 MHz clock is running.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-14 step 7. The monostable U15, with C63 and R48, is retriggered by the 4 MHz clock; while it is retriggered its Q1 output stays high. If the clock stops, C63 charges, Q1 goes low, and that low is wired to U14's preset -- which turns the shunt switch on and the series switch off and pins the filter input at REFCOM. A logic low found here with the clock present is a failed watchdog holding the DAC at zero.

probePoints.label: U14 pins 5 and 6 (Q1 and Q1*, CH1 SERIES A)
probePoints.condition: 6.5 V dc, operate. Scope at 2 V/div, 2 ms/div. TTL square wave at about 50 % duty on pin 5; pin 6 must be its complement.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-14 step 8. Pin 5 is CH1 SERIES A, which switches Q7; pin 6 is inverted by Q35 to make CH1 SHUNT and amplified by Q33/Q34 to make CH1 SERIES B. Read the step's title carefully: 'the Q1 and Q1* output of U14' names the flip-flop's outputs, not the transistor Q1, which on this board is the HR5 heater driver at the other end of the assembly.

probePoints.label: U12 pin 7 (CH2 FLOATING)
probePoints.condition: Scope at 10 V/div, 2 ms/div (Figure 5-26). Check amplitude and edge quality only.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-14 step 11. The second channel after optocoupler U12. The manual's note under Figure 5-26 says the duty cycle may differ and that at this point only the amplitude and a sharp rise and fall time are being verified -- the fine channel's duty cycle is whatever the low-order output digits ask for.

probePoints.label: U11 pin 3 (3 V source)
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-14 step 12, which asks for 'a nominal 3V dc' and gives no band; the ±5 % here is a working figure and is marked inferred. The 3 V is made from the 13 V reference: U1B follows it, a 100 kΩ / 30 kΩ pair in HR5 divides it, and U11 buffers the result. It is the amplitude the second channel switches, before a further ÷3800 in HR5 leaves the 0.78 mV the filter actually sees. The step names U1B and the HR5 resistors as the suspects, not U11.

probePoints.label: U23 pin 7 (adc input select)
probePoints.condition: 10 V dc, operate, with DAC DIAG SEL selecting DAC HI DIAG.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-15 step 1. U23 is the quad FET switch that chooses what the adc looks at. Here it has selected DAC HI DIAG, which is the 10 V DAC output divided by R79 (100 kΩ) and R84 (4.7 kΩ) -- 4.49 %, so 0.45 V. §5-15 step 14 repeats this measurement in the ADCAMP OUT SEL position, where it should instead equal the reading at TP11.

probePoints.label: U25 pin 22 (adc input)
probePoints.condition: 10 V dc, operate.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-15 step 2. The same 0.45 V one stage later, after the R74 / C84 filter that removes 60 Hz and 190 Hz and the U24 buffer. The step names U24 as the suspect, not U25: if the level is right at U23 pin 7 and wrong here, the fault is in the filter and buffer between them.

probePoints.label: U22 pin 6 (buffered DAC LO DIAG)
probePoints.condition: Standby. Common on TP1, not TP12.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-15 step 3, which gives 0 V ±11 mV. DAC LO DIAG is buffered by U22 to supply the return current for the two heater diagnostic lines, which are referenced to FR1 COM rather than to the adc's own common. It is a return path, so a few tens of millivolts here is not a small error -- it is the whole signal.

probePoints.label: U25 pin 16 (adc +7.5 V supply)
probePoints.condition: Standby. Common on TP1.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-15 step 4. VR27 shunt-regulates this from +17 SB through R77. One of only three §5-15 checks referenced to TP1 rather than TP12.

probePoints.label: U25 pin 17 (adc -8.2 V supply)
probePoints.condition: Standby. Common on TP1.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-15 step 5. The negative half of the adc chip's own supply pair, set by VR28 through R94. Note the asymmetry is deliberate: +7.5 V and -8.2 V, not a matched pair.

probePoints.label: U26 pin 7 (buffered ADC COM)
probePoints.condition: Standby.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-15 step 6, which gives 0 V ±600 mV -- a wide band, because this node is a buffered common rather than a signal. U20B and U26A cancel the current U19A puts into ADC COM.

probePoints.label: VR29 anode (adc -6.4 V reference)
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-15 step 7. VR29 is the only temperature-compensated zener on the board -- 6.4 V, 2 %, 2 ppm/°C, stock 419036 -- and it sets the adc's scale. VR30 and R91/R92/R93 bias it. A drift here is a calibration error across every range the instrument has, not a hard failure, so it is worth measuring even when nothing has been reported wrong.

probePoints.label: U27 pin 1 (adc +6.4 V reference)
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-15 step 8. The positive image of the -6.4 V reference, made by U27B inverting it. The step names U27B as the only suspect.

probePoints.label: U29 pin 7 (sample/hold +bootstrap)
probePoints.condition: Standby.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-15 step 9, which gives 'between 5.4 and 8.2V' -- recorded here as 6.8 ±1.4 V, which is the same interval. This is a bootstrapped supply that follows the held voltage, so a wide band is correct rather than sloppy. Q56, Q57 and VR31-VR34 build it.

probePoints.label: U29 pin 4 (sample/hold -bootstrap)
probePoints.condition: Standby.
probePoints.note: Printed as §5-15 step 10, published as 'between -5.4 and -8.2V'. The negative half of the same bootstrap pair and the same suspect list; the manual prints the magnitudes unsigned in the range but signs them in the step text.

probePoints.label: TP1 on the Buffered Reference SIP (A11A2)
probePoints.condition: Power-up default state. Common on TP1 of the main board, not on the SIP.
probePoints.note: Published as 'between 6.5 and 7.0V dc and very stable', so 6.75 ±0.25 V here. This is on the plug-in A11A2 assembly, not on A11: the U1A, U2A, Q3 and Q4 the step tells you to check are the SIP's own parts and share designators with quite different parts on the main board. BRF6 and its sense line BSRF6 go out to the rest of the calibrator from here. Fault code 2814 checks the same node by nulling the DAC against it and trips at 10 %.

probePoints.label: TP2 on the Buffered Reference SIP (A11A2)
probePoints.condition: Power-up default state. Common on TP1 of the main board, not on the SIP.
probePoints.note: Published as 'between 13 and 14V dc and very stable'. The buffered 13 V, made by the SIP's U1B and U2B with Q10 and Q11 from REF13 FILT, feeding BRF13 and BSRF13 to the rest of the calibrator. Same warning as the 6.5 V check: every designator §5-16 names is on the SIP. Fault code 2816 is the software equivalent.
